source_description: Putzmühle , first recorded in 1600 as one of three flour-mills of Schellerhau. 1618 "Christoph Wecks mill" with compulsory use for Schellerhau, Oberpöbel and Schönfeld. 1690–1698 stamp mill and tin-washings for a nearby tin-mine of the "Hilfe Gottes, Zwitterzeche am Pöbelberg" mining union. 1698–1912 flour-mill, owned by the naming Putze family. Destroyed by fire and re-erected in 1831. Temporarily saw-mill. 1912–1980 restaurant; 1970–1980 in state ownwership. Disused 1980–1998, then reconstructed and carried on as restaurant by Gommlich family.

source_description: The Town Hall, Market Place, Tamworth Built in 1701 by Thomas Guy, M.P. for the town. It is of mellow brick with arcades at ground level, large Jacobean windows and a steeply-pitched roof topped by a cupola. (The Shell Guide to England, 1970) It once housed the Butter Market and was used to store the towns fire engine. The rear was added in the 19th century. The Tourist Information Centre is located next to it. In front is the bronze statue of Sir Robert Peel, dating from 1852. Former Tamworth MP and twice Prime Minister, Sir Robert delivered his famous Tamworth Manifesto from the window of the Town Hall in 1834. (From the Heritage Trail leaflet) http://www.tamworth.gov.uk/PDF/heritage_trail2.pdf

Evans amongst others, a fundraiser for the Westland Pioneers' Memorial maintenance. Printed by the Hokitika Guardian. Caption: "This is the photograph of the Explorers’ Monument on its original site in Weld Street. It is now on Cemetery Hill, overlooking the Tasman Ocean. It is a memorial to Henry Whitcombe, Road Surveyor, drowned in Teremakau [ sic ] river, May 6, 1863; Charlton Howitt, Explorer, drowned Lake Brunner, September, 1863; Charles Townsend, Government Agent, drowned, Grey River, October 9, 1863; George Dobson, Surveyor, murdered, Grey-Arnold road, May 28, 1866."

source_description: Pamphlet for the 1919 exhibition of the Gruppe "RIH" collected by Georg Bredig (1868-1944). The exhibition was at Gallery Moos, an art gallery founded by Max Moos. The RIH group (1919-1920) was an artist group founded in Karlsruhe, Germany. The pamphlet lists artists Walter Becker (1893-1984), Oskar Fischer (1892-1955), Egon Itta (1890-1971), Rudolf Schlichter (1890-1955), Georg Scholz (1890-1945), Eugen Segewitz (1886-1952), and Wladimir von Zabotin (1884-1967). The group was founded on the basis of overcoming the conventions of art. Artists in the group worked closely in dadaism and cubism.

source_description: Tamworth Registration Office and Old Stone Cross public house, Church Street, Tamworth Two conflicting versions of the history of this building. ImagesofEngland states that it was first built c.1770, became a malt house in the early 19C and a Baptist chapel in 1870. The porch was added in 1908 and it became an arts centre in 1970. The heritage Trail leaflet states that it was built as a theatre in 1821, was converted into a Baptist Chapel in 1879, into a multi-purpose Arts Centre in 1974, and into the town registry records office in 1999 (The OS still caption it as an arts centre). The Old Stone Cross public house was built in the early 18C over early 16C cellars. The façade was reconstructed in 1974. Brick with some timber framing and concrete dressings. (ImagesofEngland)

source_description: US Army World War I recruiting poster by James Montgomery Flagg, with the phrase "I want you for U.S. Army," used the familiar figure of "Uncle Sam". This became the most famous and, even today still used recruiting poster by the US Army. There is a blank space below the printed phrase "Nearest recruiting station" for adding the address for enlisting. From April 1917 to autumn of 1918 more than four million pieces of it were printed. This print was probably made in 1975.

source_description: Seattle's Coliseum Theatre, at the northeast corner of Fifth Avenue and Pike Street, was the world's first theater designed just for the movies. Unlike other theaters of its time, it had no stage for live acts. It did, however, have a nursery for children, and an organ and orchestra to play with silent movies. Designed by B. Marcus Priteca (1889-1971), a noted local architect, the theater remained Seattle's premier movie house into the 1980s, when it lost out to suburban multiplexes. The Coliseum closed in 1990 but was reborn as a Banana Republic store in 1994 and maintains some of its original architectural features. This poster advertises "The Wonderful Thing," a motion picture shown at the Coliseum Theatre from November 19-25, 1921. A portrait of its star, silent film actress Norma Marie Talmadge (1894-1957), decorates this poster. Caption information source: "Coliseum Theater opens...

Peruna was an “herbal drug dissolved in a liquid made by the fermentation of juices of vegetable origin,” being about 56 - 60 proof alcohol. He also manufactured Man-U-Pi-A and Lac-O-Lin. The publisher and editor was teacher Jovan S. Jovanović, and it was printed by the State Printing House of the Kingdom of Serbia. source_description: Karadzic is a monthly newspaper, which was published in the period from 1899 to 1903 in Aleksinac. It was a paper for Serbian folk life, customs and traditions, when it was edited by the then professor of the Aleksinac teacher's school, Dr. Tihomir Djordjevic. The magazine was extremely rich in interesting texts, it was a small ethnological collection. In it, you could read how holidays were celebrated in different parts of the country, how they were spoken, what curses were like, what charms, riddles and proverbs were. You could also learn a lot about the clothes of people in different areas, about music, toasts and songs, about customs and superstition. The magazine was full of folk tales, as well as stories about the origin of the names of villages and other places.

source_description: Stradija was a satirical paper. The first issue was published on December 25, 1904, and the last on May 29, 1905. It was published in Belgrade in Serbian, printed in Cyrillic. Here, Radoje Domanović published a series of satires in prose and verse, with which he ridiculed the petty bourgeois society. A total of 50 of Domanović's texts from the Stradija newspaper were printed later in his "Complete Works". At the time of Stradija's coming to power, there were radicals to whom Domanović also belonged, so he criticized them as well.

Its origins date back to 1908, when the Provincial Association of Westphalia founded the State Museum. The aim was to collect art and cultural history from the region and make it accessible to the public. The current museum building on Domplatz was reopened in 2014 after extensive renovation. The new building, designed by the architectural firm Staab Architekten, combines historic parts of the building with modern architecture and creates spacious exhibition rooms. The collection includes works from the Middle Ages to the present day, including important paintings, sculptures, and handcrafted objects. source_description: Man-to-Man Magazine from 1910, with Prime Minister of Canada Wilfrid Laurier on the cover. This is a combined issue for July and August, which messes up the numbering of volumes and issues a bit. They continued to number subsequent issues 8, 9, and 10 in the months to follow, but jumped to number 12 for December, I guess to reassure folks they hadn't missed anything. Or maybe someone forgot about 11 altogether. Oh, and such a great illustration of Sir Wilfrid Laurier. Unfortunately, the index page doesn't seem to reveal who is credited with the cover page design. Perhaps this is revealed somewhere in the magazine? I tweaked this issue in Photoshop somewhat, adding the brown border which was mostly trimmed when the issue was bound in a volume.

source_description: Walter H. "Walt" Day (1911-2001) was an American businessman and politician. Day was born in Bradshaw, West Virginia and moved to Valdez, Alaska , in 1929. He was part of a family which purchased the former Fort Liscum and operated a cannery and other businesses on the site before it was in turn purchased by Alyeska Pipeline Service Company , which built the Valdez Marine Terminal at the terminus of the Trans-Alaska Pipeline . Day was best known for serving as mayor of Valdez for several years in the 1960s or 1970s and for being the editor-publisher of the Valdez Copper Basin News newspaper. He was also involved in the insurance and real estate businesses and with the area's rural electrification cooperative organizations.

source_description: Propaganda leaflet dropped by air, late 1917. To further illustrate the use of Turkish prisoners for British Propaganda purposes, here is another example. The note basically says: Come on over fellows, I am having a great time being a POW. This picture also demonstrates another issue. The lack of care in presentation of the subject. In this picture, the photographer made a classic error. I am not sure if it was intentional but it stands out like a wart and was sure to be picked up by the viewer. source_description: The Blood Vote - Anti-conscription handbill poem issued during anti-conscription campaign, 1917. Purportedly written by William Robert Winspear. Note: Leaflet with a verse by W. R. Winspear and a drawing by Claude Marquet, features an image a deeply worried woman casting a 'Yes' vote while Billy Hughes, Australia's labor prime minister and supporter of conscription, looks on gleefully. It was printed by Fraser & Jenkinson in Melbourne, 1917 and authorised by J. Curtin, Secretary for the 'National Executive'. 'The Blood Vote' was widely-published in papers such as The Australian Worker, The Westralian Worker and The Catholic Press. It was also posted directly into letterboxes.

source_description: Politički glasnik is a magazine that was published once a week, in the period from 1925 to 1927 in Belgrade. It was a political magazine, which critically covered all current political topics, both domestic and foreign. The political messenger set out to follow political life in its not only public but also hidden relations every week, in short and lively articles, noting all its interesting facts and anecdotes, and presenting to the public the behind-the-scenes work of parties and politicians. The editor and director of this magazine was Momir Nikolić, and the owner was Đordje Perić. One of the editors was also Dr. Vladislav Stakić.

ocr_or_excerpt: Politički glasnik is a magazine that was published once a week, in the period from 1925 to 1927 in Belgrade. It was a political magazine, which critically covered all current political topics, both domestic and foreign. The political messenger set out to follow political life in its not only public but also hidden relations every week, in short and lively articles, noting all its interesting facts and anecdotes, and presenting to the public the behind-the-scenes work of parties and politicians. The editor and director of this magazine was Momir Nikolić, and the owner was Đordje Perić. One of the editors was also Dr. Vladislav Stakić.

The political messenger set out to follow political life in its not only public but also hidden relations every week, in short and lively articles, noting all its interesting facts and anecdotes, and presenting to the public the behind-the-scenes work of parties and politicians. The editor and director of this magazine was Momir Nikolić, and the owner was Đordje Perić. One of the editors was also Dr. Vladislav Stakić.

source_description: Mustul care fierbe ("The Frothing Must"), political cartoon mocking the Romanian nationalist politico Octavian Goga. Titled after, and jokingly misquoting, Goga's political pamphlet of the same name, it was published just prior to the December 1933 parliamentary election. Goga is in the foreground; the other figure is an unnamed journalist interviewing him. Journalist to Goga: Am impresia că asist la preludiile unei mari agitaţii... After all this time [i.e.: out of the spotlight] I still get thirsty for must!") Reference to Goga's 1927 essay of that title, which argued that "the [antisemitic] Roumanian student movement is only the wine of Roumanian Nationalism in fermentation" (I. Yevin, "What May the Jew Expect...

Fez o relatório o 1.º tenente Baartel Taerlink e, um ano depois, uma equipagem inglesa comandada por John Lethbridge levantava uma parte do carregamento, então de somente 346 barras. source_description: Tellurium Locality: Faţa Băii (Facebánya), Zlatna (Zalatna; Zalathna) , Alba County , Romania ( Locality at mindat.org ) Size: 5.5 x 3.7 x 1.5 cm (pillbox). An old-time specimen of 7-9 grains of native tellurium in an antique packaging. The tellurium grains are in a 2.9 cm, cotton-stoppered, broken glass test tube. The test tube is in a matchbox-like, laxative pillbox that says: New Labeling Adopted 1939. An old handwritten label, along with a faded English label is included in the box. I believe this classic material is from the type locality of Facebanya, not Felsobanya (Baia Sprie) as the more modern labels indicate. I think that the old label showing Facebanja was mistaken for the same as Felsobanya. Offenbanya is an old, historic telluride district, while Felsobanya, according to Mindat, does not include native tellurium. Facebanja, however, surely did...first. Ex. Dennis Mullane...

The Wehrmacht propaganda section (OKW/WPr) produced an imitation in green, serial number H86D729630, signed "Peppiatt." For years it was believed that this was a copy of the British green one pound note. However, close examination of the background indicates a diamond pattern at the top and bottom that is found on the pink and blue note. The Germans apparently printed this parody in the wrong color. All evidence points to the Luftwaffe dropping these notes in November and December of 1942 over a 200-mile area of Northern Egypt that included Cairo, Alexandria and El Alamein. source_description: Pidgin English leaflet, which was drop over New Guinea from Allied aircraft, on display at the RAAF Museum. The leaflet reads: ALL LULUAIS, TULTULS AND GOVERNMENT BOYS. We have defeated the Japanese and gained control of Salamaua, Lae and Finschafen. Most of the Japanese soldiers are marooned and they want to force you to help them and work for them. You know that in the past theu have hurt and abused many locals from Rabaul in the manner, also some locals have been by our powerful bombs. Keep away from the Japanese, there is no need for you to be killed for nothing. If you get this message out soldiers are nearby, so some and fine the Patrol Officer who is with them. The Government says this.

source_description: "Car of the Future" as conceived by Studebaker's Director of Styling, Raymond Loewy , in the August 1950 issue of Science and Mechanics . Loewy wrote about the new styling for "tomorrow's rocket age population" but dismissed the idea of clear plastic tops and turbine engines. The three point front end was a design feature on the 1951 Studebaker . Some of the other elements of this concept model influenced the 1953 Studebaker Starliner . The cover art was done by Arthur C. Bade, a staff illustrator for Science and Mechanics from 1944 to 1955. This magazine cover was lightly soiled and had a few minor folds, scratches and cuts. It was scanned with an Epson Perfection V500 scanner and saved as a 400 dpi tiff file. The restoration was done in Adobe Photoshop Elements. The magazine size is 6.5 by 9.25 inches (165 by 235 mm) and has 224 pages.

source_description: US Army University, Shrivenham, England, UK, 1945 British women advise students at the US Army University, Shrivenham on various issues. Amongst the GIs seeking advice are Corporal Wilfred Hoenninger, in the foreground, being shown a leaflet about the city of Cambridge by Meredydd Saunders-Davies. Next in line (moving away from the camera) is Captain Edward K Austin, who wishes to go to Scotland. According to the original caption, "dark-haired Diana Phipps perched on stool in background is a niece of the Duchess of Gloucester". In the foreground, another GI looks at a pile of copies of the 'Shrivenham Post', the university newspaper.

It is known as the Golden or Gilded Chapel because of its three gilded retables and other decor. The French name of the chapel is La Chapelle de Notre-Dame de Pouey-Laun. The chapel was classified as a Historic Monument in September 1954. It is almost a compulsory visit for anyone passing through the spectacular Azun Valley. The key is available at the Tourism Office in Arrens-Marsous. The chapel is of uncertain origins, but there is more than one legend. The leaflet available in the chapel mentions a statue in a great light; Wikipedia claims an apparition of the Virgin led to its foundation. source_description: Sun City is a census-designated place and unincorporated town in Maricopa County, Arizona, United States, that is within the Phoenix metropolitan area. The population was 37,499 according to the 2010 census. Its adjoining sister city is Sun City West. Both cities are retirement communities popular with snowbirds. Sun City was opened January 1, 1960, with five home models, a shopping center, a recreation center, and a golf course. The opening weekend drew 100,000 people, ten times more than expected, and resulted in a Time magazine cover story. The future retirement community was built on the site of the former ghost town of Marinette. Developer Del E. Back page text reads: "Easily recognisable, the new traffic signal at PANDA CROSSINGS is always accompanied by triangular shaped black and white markings across the road: those on Zebra crossings are rectangular. In addition, the post carries a yellow globe with black horizontal stripes. Two panels on the signal post each carry a push-button for pedestrians to press when they want to cross. "For details of the proper way to use these crossings please see the middle page of this leaflet. "This is a one-year experiment. "Prepared by the Ministry of Transport and the Central Office of Information."

Rostock, Überseehafen, Kisten, Container ADN-ZB Sindermann 20.4.1973 - Rostock MS "Freundschaft" wird Solidaritätsfracht nach Haiphong bringen. Das DDR-Motorschiff "Freundschaft" wird in der nächsten Woche in Rostock die Leinen losmachen und Kurs auf Haiphong nehmen - mit einer Solidaritätsfracht im Werte von mehreren Millionen Mark an Bord. Auch über die Osterfeiertage wird zügig beladen, um ein rechtzeitiges "In See stechen" zu garantieren. Unser Bild zeigt einen Teil der in Kisten und Containern angelieferten Güter am Kai vor der "Freundschaft".

source_description: United States Navy GMLS Mark 11 Mod 2 port side missile launcher aboard USS Chicago (CG-11), circa in 1970. The RIM-24 Tartar magazines aboard Albany -class cruisers overhung the sides of the ship requiring safety nets visible outboard of the launcher. The blue missiles with white wings were dummy testing missiles used for display purposes. The circular hatch visible below the nearer missile is a door to vertical magazine cells below the launcher accessed by rotating the circular magazine cover and launcher over the cell to be loaded. The rectangular hatch visible on the deck behind the launcher was used to transfer RIM-8 Talos missiles into the forward Talos magazine.

source_description: Nui Dat, South Vietnam. June 1970. One of the leaflets prepared by the 1st Psychological Operations Unit, the newest unit of the 1st Australian Task Force (1ATF). The leaflet tells the VC to hide their weapons and either to go to the South Vietnamese Government Forces or Allied Forces, or hide with a friend and ask him to contact the Government for help. The leaflets emphasise that if the instructions are followed, they will be safe.

Founded in 1972, HULA Animal Rescue purchased a 17 acre smallholding just outside the village of Aspley Guise in Bedfordshire in 1976 and built the Sanctuary which was officially opened in early 1978. The Sanctuary takes in unwanted and abandoned animals from Milton Keynes and the surrounding area, helping animals from as far afield as the Home Counties and the Midlands. It provides temporary shelter for dogs, cats and small animals until such time as new homes can be found for them. source_description: Looking NNW from Portland Canal just above McAlpine Locks . In foreground, props (A-frames) for Boule movable dam are stacked on barge. Towboat "Wayne McBride" with crane barges. . Twin screw towboat "Wayne McBride" (doc. # 554585, length 60 feet, breadth 22 feet, D353 Marine Brochure Specifications.pdf Caterpillar D353TA diesels (?), 850 hp). Built in 1974 by Serodino, Inc. , Guild, Tennessee . Originally named "Delta Dawn", owned by Flowers Transportation, Greenville, Mississippi. In 1979, sold to Arkansas River Co., Greenville. In 1981, renamed "Martha Amee" . In 1991, sold to Five M Transportation Corp. , Louisville, Kentucky, and renamed "Wayne McBride". Still operating in 2017. . Ohio River mile 606. Louisville, Kentucky . Jan. 25, 2001. file # a1a045. . Scanned from 6x9 cm E-6 transparency taken with Fuji GW690 II (90 mm lens) or Fuji GSW690 III (65 mm lens).

source_description: Salem Sue (or The World's Largest Holstein Cow) is a giant fiberglass Holstein cow sculpture located in New Salem, North Dakota, United States. Salem Sue was built in 1974 for $40,000. The project was sponsored by the New Salem Lions Club in honor of the local dairy farming industry. The artist was Dave Oswald and the construction was done by Sculpture Mfg. Co in La Crosse, Wisconsin. The statue stands 38 feet (12 m) high and 50 feet (15 m) long. It sits on School Hill near Interstate 94 off exit 127 S and can be viewed for several miles. Salem Sue was the second giant roadside animal sculpture built in North Dakota. A road leads up to the base of the statue, where one may view the surrounding terrain for a distance of several miles. source_description: A Glimpse into the Production of a Facsimile: The photo shows Charlotte Kramer (Müller & Schindler/Universal Art Group) during quality control in the bookbinding workshop. The focus is on the precise bookbinding work being done on the cover for the edition Of Plants and Animals. The photograph documents the process in which traditional craftsmanship and quality standards converge to ensure that the cover feels true to the original and is built to last.

source_description: On 2 September 1980 this leaflet was sent to the Auckland office of the Lands and Survey Department. At this time New Zealand was experiencing an oil supply crisis. The sale of petrol was banned at weekends, the open-road speed limit had been cut to 80 kph, and a policy of “carless days” had been tried from 30 July 1979, but abandoned in May 1980. Another measure to conserve petrol was the conversion of Government vehicles to run on CNG [compressed natural gas]. Mostly this involved the vehicles being able to run on CNG or petrol. The government made interest-free loans available for the conversions, and also offered subsidies for the construction of refuelling stations. At the peak of its use, about 10% of New Zealand cars had been converted. The page shown here is from a leaflet included in a Lands and Survey file held in Auckland Regional Office - Conservation of fuel - energy...

source_description: A Post Medieval copper alloy book fitting – book clasp (late 16th century). This rectangular book clasp has a flat hook projecting from one end (to hook into a corresponding ‘eye’ piece) and the other end expands and has a central rivet hole for attachment to the book cover. The expanded end is also decorated with two triangular notches along the outer edge. There is another rivet, still in situ, just in front of the hook and possibly the remains of a third iron rivet near the first rivet hole. The front surface is decorated with irregular engraved lines running along the length of the clasp. There is a tiny fragment of sheet metal concreted to the reverse of the clasp near the rivet at the hook end. This plate was possibly, originally, secured by this rivet. source_description: Note on discovery: all the small finds, except one coin, were found within a lead container (no. 198 below), at a depth of about 18 inches, while five of the larger, complete arm-rings were found underneath it. The objects are described in their uncleaned condition, in accordance with the terms of the Treasure Act 1996, and some of the details are currently obscured by adhering soil. After conservation, some of the weights may be slightly lighter, although there is unlikely to be any significant difference. Surface metal analysis of a sample of six objects from the hoard conducted at the British Museum indicated approximate metal contents, as follows:- Arm-ring (no. 1) - silver 97% with 2% copper Arm-ring (no. 2) - silver 93% with 3% copper Arm-ring (no. 4) - silver 97% with 2% copper; the central collet - 95% silver with 3% copper; and tongue-shaped collet - 95% silver with 2% copper...

Stipules are strongly toothed and hairy on the lower surface. Flowerheads are 2–5-flowered; the peduncle is shorter than subtending petiole. Calyx teeth are equal in length to the calyx tube and the corolla is yellow. Flowers in spring.
